AFTER THE FACT -- what V2 actually says, and turning the bound into an impossibility
(i) V2 FAILED ON ONE THRESHOLD OF THREE, and the pattern is the result.
>= 1.5x   protein-only  575 : mRNA-only  135  = 4.3:1   p 1.80e-65   (710 discordant genes)
>= 2.0x   protein-only  139 : mRNA-only   78  = 1.8:1   p 4.16e-05   (217 discordant genes)
>= 3.0x   protein-only   39 : mRNA-only   35  = 1.1:1   p 7.28e-01   (74 discordant genes)
Overwhelming at 1.5x and 2x, gone at 3x where only 74 genes remain discordant.
The asymmetry is REAL and it is FIVE TIMES WEAKER than the camera reported:
1.8:1 by mass spectrometry against 9.5:1 by imaging.
(ii) THE CAMERA OVER-CALLS BY SEVENFOLD, and geometry is not why.
MS confirms 42 of 315 imaging-CCD genes (13.3%) against 1.4% of the imaging-non-CCD controls -- a real 9.6x
enrichment, so the camera is not making it up. But it calls seven proteins
cell-cycle-dependent for every one the spectrometer confirms.
Dual localisation is 88.6% in the disconfirmed set and 88.1% in
the confirmed set -- a +0.5% difference at p = 1.0000. It separates
imaging-CCD from imaging-control (+19.5%, p 0.0000) but NOT true calls from
false ones, so it is a property of what the imaging pipeline scores, not a
mechanism that turns movement into apparent abundance. The hypothesis is retired.
(iii) THE AMPLITUDE BOUND, MADE WAVEFORM-FREE -- and it finally separates the two terms.
loops 121-122 measured the bound as beta*gain(bbar,T) for a SINUSOIDAL drive. That
is the wrong shape for the biology: a real destruction switch is a PULSE, and a
pulse reaches a larger amplitude than a sine of the same mean without any rate ever
going negative. So the sinusoidal number understates what production can do, and
the bound is redone here for an ARBITRARY non-negative drive.
PRODUCTION SIDE, exactly. For dP/dt = k(t) - b*P with k(t) >= 0 of any shape, the
extreme is bang-bang: 2*kbar for half the cycle, 0 for the other half. Solving the
periodic steady state gives max relative amplitude = tanh(b*T/4), full stop. It
depends ONLY on the measured half-life and the cycle length -- no drive parameter,
no waveform, nothing to fit. Transcription and translation are both production, so
this one bound covers everything loops 119, 120 and 122 tested.
DEGRADATION SIDE. b(t) has no upper limit -- destruction can be arbitrarily fast --
so it is NOT bounded by tanh(b*T/4) and can in principle reach 1.0. That asymmetry
is the whole point: an oscillation above tanh(b*T/4) cannot come from the
production side at all, and REQUIRES regulated degradation.
80 genes oscillate >= 2-fold by MS and have a measured half-life
observed relative amplitude: median 0.445
production ceiling tanh(b*T/4): median 0.284, range 0.156-0.810
EXCEED THE PRODUCTION CEILING: 55 of 80 = 68.8%
For those, no transcriptional or translational mechanism of ANY waveform can
produce the oscillation that was measured. Regulated degradation is not one
hypothesis among several for them -- it is the only term left in the equation.
(the sinusoid-specific statistic, reported for continuity with loops 121-122:
median beta 2.35, beta > 1 for 86.2% -- larger, because a sine is the weakest usable waveform)
The half-lives are NIH3T3 mouse and the proteins are human NB4, which is what makes
the two measurements independent and is also the main caveat on this number.
